data.title: Vice Foreign Minister Stresses International Cooperation to Safeguard Maritime Routes
data.content:
Naples, November 20, 2026, SPA -- Vice Minister of Foreign Affairs Waleed Elkhereiji participated on Thursday in a session titled "The Revenge of Geography: Securing Chokepoints, Rethinking Maritime Security," held on the sidelines of the MED – Mediterranean Dialogues conference in Naples, Italy.
    During the session, Elkhereiji said recent developments along maritime routes have underscored the close link between maritime security, regional stability, and global prosperity. He noted that the security of strategic waterways, from the Red Sea and the Bab al-Mandab Strait to the Strait of Hormuz, is a matter of international concern. Protecting these vital routes, he stressed, remains a longstanding priority requiring effective regional and international cooperation.
    He emphasized the importance of diplomacy, de-escalation, and addressing the root causes of regional instability to keep vital waterways safe and open in accordance with international law.
    Regarding Yemen, Elkhereiji reaffirmed Saudi Arabia's continued efforts to promote security and prosperity in the country. He stressed the need to counter any attempts to use Yemeni territory to threaten neighboring countries or international shipping.
    He also affirmed the Kingdom's legitimate right to defend its territory, people, and national interests in accordance with international law.
    -- SPA
